Opening Invoke in another tab, or reloading another tab, then takes over the unsaved changes a still-open tab is holding: an edit whose save had not finished when the tab was hidden, or one kept while the server was unreachable. The second tab saves them, and undoing the edit in the first tab no longer removes it. **Workaround:** Open Invoke over HTTPS, or at `localhost` on the computer running it, where browsers provide Web Locks.

# Canvas guide

> A detailed guide to the Canvas — its tools and their options, navigation, the header buttons, the generation frame, selections, transform, filters, the staging area, menus, settings and keyboard shortcuts.

This page describes the Canvas itself: its tools, controls and menus. For an introduction to working with the Canvas, see [Crafting images with the Canvas](/users-guide/canvas/introduction/). The Layers panel, where layers and their settings are managed, has its own [guide](/users-guide/canvas/layers-panel/). Each project has one canvas. It opens in the center of the **Edit** layout (**Alt+2**), or press **2** to bring it to the front. ![The Canvas with its tool strip on the left and the header buttons along the top: zoom, fit buttons, undo and redo, save, new canvas, settings and more.](/_astro/canvas-toolbar.DAPl8T8M_jH1At.webp) ## Tools [Section titled “Tools”](#tools) The tool strip on the left edge of the canvas holds the drawing and editing tools. A tool’s options appear in the **Tool** section of the **Properties** tab in the Layers panel, not on the canvas. | Tool | Key | What it does | | ------------------------------------- | ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **View** | **H** | Pan by dragging. Hold **Space** to pan from any tool. | | **Move** | **V** | Move the selected layers. **Shift** locks the direction. Dragging inside a selection lifts the selected pixels so you can move them; **Enter** places them. | | **Transform** | **Ctrl+T** | Scale and rotate the selected layer with handles. See [Transforming layers](#transforming-layers). | | **Generation frame** | **C** | Move and resize the generation frame. Tap **C** to switch to it, or hold **C** to use it briefly. | | **Brush** | **B** | Paint on the selected raster layer, or paint a mask or region on the selected inpaint mask or regional guidance layer. | | **Eraser** | **E** | Erase paint or mask. | | **Shape** | **R** | Draw a rectangle, ellipse, triangle, star, polygon or freehand shape on a raster layer, or add a shaped area to the selected inpaint mask or regional guidance layer. Press **R** again to cycle through the shapes. | | **Gradient** | **G** | Create a linear or radial gradient. | | **Text** | **T** | Add editable text. | | **Marquee select** / **Lasso select** | **U** / **L** | Select an area of pixels. Press **U** again to switch between rectangle and ellipse, or **L** again for freehand and polygon. | The Shape and Select buttons hold several tools. Click to use the current one, or press and hold (or right-click, or press **→** on) the button to choose another from a menu that lists each tool with its shortcut. To pick a color from the canvas, hold **Alt** with any painting tool and click. While you pick, a round **loupe** follows the pointer: it magnifies the pixels around it, boxes the pixel that will be picked in the center, and shows that pixel’s RGB values. The pointer itself is hidden, so aim with the boxed pixel. You can drag to sample as you go; the color is set when you release. ### Tool options [Section titled “Tool options”](#tool-options) * **Brush** — **Size**, **Opacity** and **Hardness**; the **Foreground** color; and, under **Dynamics**, whether pen pressure affects the width or the opacity. **\[** and **]** make the brush smaller or larger, and so does **Ctrl**+scroll. * **Eraser** — **Size**, **Opacity** and **Hardness**. * **Shape** — the **Kind** of shape; **Place on**, which draws on the **Selected layer** or on a **New layer** of its own; **Fill** and **Stroke**, each with a color; and the stroke **Width**. **Shift** constrains the proportions. For polygons, click to place points and double-click, press **Enter** or click the first point to close the shape. With an inpaint mask or regional guidance layer selected, the shape is added to the mask or region, which makes shapes a quick way to mark rectangular or geometric areas; the colors are ignored. * **Gradient** — **Kind** (Linear or Radial), **Angle**, and the color **Stops**, which can be added and removed or follow the foreground and background colors. Dragging creates a gradient layer the size of the generation frame, or repositions the selected gradient layer. * **Text** — the font **Family**, **Style** or **Weight**, **Size**, **Line height**, **Align** and **Fill** color. Click the canvas to start typing; **Ctrl+Enter** or clicking elsewhere finishes the text, and **Escape** cancels it. The text stays editable as a text layer. * **Marquee select** and **Lasso select** — the **Shape** and the selection **Mode** (Replace, Add, Subtract or Intersect). **Shift** adds to the selection and **Alt** subtracts from it. The **Actions** fill or erase the selection, lift it to a **New layer**, **Invert** it, select everything, or **Deselect**. ### Fonts [Section titled “Fonts”](#fonts) The Text tool offers built-in font families, plus any fonts you add. To add fonts, open **Fonts** in the Launchpad and use **Add Fonts** to upload `.ttf`, `.otf`, `.woff` or `.woff2` files. Uploaded fonts are private to your account (**My fonts**); administrators can also upload shared fonts for everyone on the server. Select a font in the library to preview it and see its variation axes and named instances. Variable fonts expose those axes in the Text tool’s options. Fonts placed in the server’s fonts directory are also available to everyone. It is `fonts` in the InvokeAI root folder by default and can be changed with `fonts_dir` in `invokeai.yaml`. It may contain subfolders. Refresh the app after adding or removing files there. If a project uses a font that is not installed, a dialog lets you retry, upload the font, or choose a replacement. You can keep editing with a marked fallback, but generating or saving the affected text needs the font. When you export a project, **Include font files** bundles the fonts it uses, if you have the right to redistribute them. Selections restrict painting: while an area is selected, brush strokes stay inside it. **Ctrl+A** selects all, **Ctrl+D** deselects and **Ctrl+Shift+I** inverts the selection. ## Navigating the canvas [Section titled “Navigating the canvas”](#navigating-the-canvas) * **Zoom** with the mouse wheel, which zooms around the pointer, or choose a level from the zoom menu in the header (25% to 500%). * **Pan** with the View tool, by holding **Space**, or by dragging with the middle mouse button. * **Fit to view** (header) fits the generation frame and all layers into the window. ## The header [Section titled “The header”](#the-header) The buttons along the top of the canvas, from left to right: * **Zoom level** and **Fit to view**. * **Fit frame to layers** (**Shift+N**) — resizes the generation frame to enclose all layers. * **Fit frame to masks** (**Shift+B**) — resizes the generation frame to enclose the inpaint masks. * **Undo canvas edit** (**Ctrl+Z**) and **Redo canvas edit** (**Ctrl+Shift+Z** or **Ctrl+Y**). * **Save Canvas to Gallery** — saves the visible canvas as an image on the Gallery’s selected board. Its arrow offers **Save BBox to Gallery**, which saves only what is inside the generation frame. * **New session → New canvas** — clears all layers and starts a fresh canvas with an empty inpaint mask. This cannot be undone. * **Canvas settings** — see [below](#canvas-settings). ## The generation frame [Section titled “The generation frame”](#the-generation-frame) The generation frame is the area that is generated. With the **Generation frame** tool selected, drag inside the frame to move it and drag its handles to resize it. **Shift** keeps the proportions, **Ctrl** resizes from the center, and **Alt** turns off snapping to the model’s grid. ![The Generation frame tool's options: Position X and Y, and the Frame's Size and Aspect with a lock button.](/_astro/canvas-frame-properties.BUym6soa_Z1F6x7Q.webp) The tool’s options show the frame’s **Position** and **Size**, and an **Aspect** menu for common aspect ratios, with a lock. The frame’s size is the generation size, so it matches the **Size** section of the Generate panel, and it snaps to the sizes the selected model supports. ### What the model sees [Section titled “What the model sees”](#what-the-model-sees) When you press **Invoke**, the enabled raster content inside the frame is combined into the image the model starts from. Content outside the frame is not included, even though it remains visible on the canvas. Control layers and regional guidance are likewise read only inside the frame. This makes placement important. If the model needs to continue a shape, match a texture or keep part of a subject, include enough of it inside the frame to give the model context. Moving the frame changes which part of the image the next generation can use. The frame is not a mask: everything inside it can change in image-to-image. To regenerate only part of the area, add an [inpaint mask](/users-guide/canvas/introduction/#inpainting). ### Frame size and processing size [Section titled “Frame size and processing size”](#frame-size-and-processing-size) The frame is the final footprint of the generation on the canvas. With **Render at** (at the bottom of the Generate panel’s **Size** section; legacy versions called it *Scale before processing*) set to **Optimal for model** or **Custom**, InvokeAI generates at a different resolution, such as the model’s optimal size, and then resizes the result to fit the frame. When the two differ, the Size section’s badge shows both, frame first, and its preview outlines the render size with a dashed line. **Optimal for model** only enlarges a frame smaller than the model’s optimal size; it never shrinks a larger one. Choose a frame large enough to include the context the model needs, while keeping it within a size the model and your GPU memory handle well. **Optimal for model** is the default, including for older projects that never saved a choice. Those projects previously generated at the frame’s size. Processing at a different resolution can change the result for the same seed, generation time, and GPU memory use. To generate at the frame’s exact size, choose **Frame size**; saved choices are preserved. ## Transforming layers [Section titled “Transforming layers”](#transforming-layers) Choose **Transform** from a layer’s menu, or press **Ctrl+T**, to scale and rotate the selected layer: * Drag a corner or edge handle to scale. **Shift** scales proportionally and **Alt** scales from the center. * Drag just outside a corner to rotate. **Shift** rotates in 15° steps. * Drag inside to move. Press **Enter** or click **Apply** to finish, or **Escape** or **Cancel** to undo the transform. The **Transform** tab of the Layers panel sets the position, scale and rotation numerically. A negative scale flips the layer. To crop a layer to the generation frame, choose **Crop layer to bbox** from its menu. **Fit to bbox** scales a layer to fit inside the frame. ## Filters and object selection [Section titled “Filters and object selection”](#filters-and-object-selection) **Filter**, in a layer’s menu or its Properties, processes a raster or control layer. Starting it opens the Layers panel’s **Properties** tab, headed *Operation: Filter*, where you choose and preview the filter. The filters are grouped by purpose: * **Edge detection** — Canny, HED, Lineart, Lineart Anime, MLSD, PiDiNet and Scribble. * **Depth & normal** — Depth Anything and Normal map. * **Pose & face** — DW Openpose and Mediapipe Face. * **Color & tone** — Color map and Adjust image. * **Blur & noise** — Content shuffle, Blur and Noise. * **Upscale** — an upscaling model. Choose a filter and its settings in Properties, click **Process** (or turn on **Process automatically**) to preview the result, then **Apply** it. The arrow next to Apply offers **Apply as** a new raster or control layer instead. Edge, depth and pose filters produce the guide images that control layers need. **Select object**, in a layer’s menu, finds an object automatically with a segmentation model. Its settings open in the **Properties** tab, headed *Operation: Select Object*. Click the object to add points (Shift-click marks areas to exclude), or describe it by text, then **Process** and **Apply**, or save the result as a selection or a new layer. ## Running a workflow on a layer [Section titled “Running a workflow on a layer”](#running-a-workflow-on-a-layer) **Run workflow**, in a raster or control layer’s menu, processes the layer with the project’s active workflow, the one open in the workflow editor. In the **Run workflow from layer** dialog, choose: * **Workflow image input** — the workflow’s image field that receives the layer. * **Workflow image output** — the node whose image is the result. * **Destination** — **Canvas staging**, **Replace layer**, **Copy as raster layer**, or **Gallery**. Then click **Run**. If the workflow has no image input and output it can connect, the dialog says so. The layer must be enabled, unlocked and not empty. ## The staging area [Section titled “The staging area”](#the-staging-area) When the Canvas is the destination, results appear in the staging area at the bottom of the canvas, not directly on it. The staging bar lets you: * Step through the results with the arrows, or with **←** and **→**, and show or hide the result thumbnails. * **Accept to Layer** — add the current result as a new raster layer at the top of the raster layers and close the staging area. * A selected inpaint mask, regional guidance or control layer that you can still edit stays selected, so you can carry on painting it. Otherwise the new layer is selected. * While the rest of the result’s batch is still queued or generating, accepting also cancels those remaining images. The batch then shows as cancelled in the queue, and undoing the accepted layer does not restart it. * The arrow next to it offers **Keep as Hidden Layer**, which adds the result as a disabled layer and keeps staging open and the batch running. * **Save to gallery** the current result, **Discard** it (**Delete**), or **Discard All**. * Hide the preview of the current result to compare it with the canvas underneath. * **Auto-switch** — show each new result as it arrives (**Newest**), follow the one in progress (**In progress**), or stay on the current one (**Off**). * **Cancel** the running generation. Right-click a result’s thumbnail to recall its settings into the Generate panel. While results are staged or a canvas generation is running, only the View tool works. ## The canvas menu [Section titled “The canvas menu”](#the-canvas-menu) Right-click the canvas to open the menu of the selected layer, the same menu as in the Layers panel (see the [Layers panel guide](/users-guide/canvas/layers-panel/#the-layer-menu)), with two extra submenus: ![The canvas right-click menu for a raster layer, with the layer actions followed by a Canvas section with Save to Gallery and Create From BBox.](/_astro/canvas-context-menu.Ba4fwzK__Z6uMD5.webp) * **Save to Gallery** — **Save Canvas to Gallery** or **Save BBox to Gallery**. * **Create From BBox** — copy what is inside the generation frame into a **New Global Reference Image**, **New Regional Reference Image**, **New Control Layer** or **New Raster Layer**. With no layer selected, the menu has only these two submenus. ## Canvas settings [Section titled “Canvas settings”](#canvas-settings) The gear button in the header opens the canvas settings. They are saved with the project. ![The Canvas settings popover with Behavior, Display and Grid options.](/_astro/canvas-settings.C8omzvVG_Z2fmpK4.webp) * **Behavior** * **Invert scroll for brush size** — reverses **Ctrl**+scroll brush sizing. * **Clip strokes to bbox** — keeps painting inside the generation frame. * **Output only generated regions** — when on, an inpainting or outpainting result contains only the regenerated area, with the rest transparent; when off, it includes the whole frame. * **Display** * **Show progress on canvas** — shows the image forming while it generates. * **Show bbox overlay** — dims everything outside the generation frame. * **Show generation frame** — shows the frame’s dashed outline. * **Checkerboard background** — shows transparent areas as a checkerboard. * **Grid** * **Show grid** — shows the model’s size grid. * **Snap to grid** — snaps the generation frame, moves and transforms to the grid. Hold **Alt** to override it. * **Rule of thirds** — shows composition guides inside the frame. ## Saving and sharing a canvas [Section titled “Saving and sharing a canvas”](#saving-and-sharing-a-canvas) The canvas belongs to its project and is saved with it automatically. To keep a finished image, use **Save Canvas to Gallery** or **Save BBox to Gallery**, or accept results and save individual layers with **Save layer to uploads**. To share a whole canvas, with its layers, masks and settings, export the project as an `.invk` file; see [Projects](/users-guide/projects/introduction/#exporting-and-importing). ## Copying and pasting [Section titled “Copying and pasting”](#copying-and-pasting) * **Ctrl+C** copies the selected pixels, and **Ctrl+X** cuts them. * **Ctrl+V** pastes an image from the clipboard as a new raster layer at the generation frame. * **Ctrl+J** duplicates the selected layer, or copies the selected pixels to a new layer. ## Keyboard shortcuts [Section titled “Keyboard shortcuts”](#keyboard-shortcuts) These shortcuts work while the canvas has focus. On macOS, use **Cmd** in place of **Ctrl**. | Shortcut | Action | | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | | **H**, **V**, **Ctrl+T**, **C**, **B**, **E**, **R**, **G**, **T**, **U**, **L** | Select a tool (see [Tools](#tools)) | | Hold **Space** | Pan temporarily | | Hold **Alt** | Pick a color | | **\[** / **]** | Smaller / larger brush or eraser | | **X** / **D** | Swap colors / reset colors to black and white | | **Ctrl+Z** / **Ctrl+Shift+Z**, **Ctrl+Y** | Undo / redo | | **Ctrl+A** / **Ctrl+D** / **Ctrl+Shift+I** | Select all / deselect / invert the selection | | **Ctrl+C** / **Ctrl+X** / **Ctrl+V** | Copy / cut / paste | | **Delete** | Erase the selection, or delete the selected layer | | **Shift+C** | Clear the selected mask | | Arrow keys (**Shift**: 10 px) | Nudge the selected layer | | **Ctrl+J** / **Ctrl+E** | Duplicate layer / merge layer down | | **Ctrl+G** / **Ctrl+Shift+G** | Group / ungroup layers | | **Ctrl+]** / **Ctrl+\[** (add **Shift** for front / back) | Move layer forward / backward | | **Alt+\[** / **Alt+]** | Previous / next layer, or staged result | | **Shift+H** | Hide control, guidance and mask layers | | **Shift+N** / **Shift+B** | Fit the generation frame to the layers / to the masks | | **Enter** / **Escape** | Apply / cancel a transform, text or filter | Some canvas commands listed in **Settings → Hotkeys** are marked *Pending*; they are not available yet.

# Crafting images with the Canvas

> An introduction to the Canvas — layers and masks, sending generations to the Canvas, inpainting, outpainting, regional prompts, control layers, drawing and adding gallery images.

The **Canvas** is where you build and refine an image in layers. You can paint, repaint part of an image (inpainting), extend it beyond its edges (outpainting), guide different regions with their own prompts, and steer the composition with control images, generating as many times as you like and keeping only the results you want. The Canvas lives in the **Edit** layout (**Alt+2**): the Canvas is in the center, the **Generate** panel on the left supplies the model, prompt and settings, and the **Layers** panel on the right lists the canvas’s layers and their settings. ![The Edit layout: the Generate panel on the left, the Canvas with a mountain landscape in the center, and the Layers panel with its color picker, layer list and Properties on the right.](/_astro/canvas-edit-layout.DBjbrvi4_1FbmNO.webp) This page introduces the main ideas and tasks. The [Canvas guide](/users-guide/canvas/canvas-guide/) and the [Layers panel guide](/users-guide/canvas/layers-panel/) describe every tool, menu and setting. ## Canvas concepts [Section titled “Canvas concepts”](#canvas-concepts) ### Layers [Section titled “Layers”](#layers) A canvas is a stack of layers. Each layer has a type, which decides what it contributes to a generation: | Layer type | What it is for | | --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Raster layer** | Ordinary image content: pictures, painting, shapes, gradients and text. The visible raster content inside the generation frame is the starting image for a generation. | | **Inpaint mask** | Marks the area to regenerate. Everything outside the mask is kept. | | **Regional guidance** | Marks an area that gets its own prompt, and optionally its own reference image, so different parts of the image can be described differently. | | **Control layer** | Holds a guide image, such as edges, a depth map or a pose, that a control model uses to shape the composition. | The Layers panel groups layers by type, in the stacks **Inpaint Masks**, **Regional Guidance**, **Control Layers** and **Raster Layers**. Within a stack, higher layers are drawn over lower ones. Add a layer with the **+** button above the layer list: ![The Add layer menu with Inpaint mask, Regional guidance, Regional reference image, Control layer, Raster layer and New group.](/_astro/canvas-add-layer-menu.CrQgOM2V_Z2aMbo7.webp) Each layer row has a dot on the left that switches the layer on or off for generation. Masks, regional guidance and control layers also have an eye button, which only hides them from view: a hidden mask still affects generation. **Shift+H** hides all of them at once so you can see the image underneath. ### Settings live in the Properties pane [Section titled “Settings live in the Properties pane”](#settings-live-in-the-properties-pane) Each layer’s settings, such as a regional prompt or a control layer’s model, are in the **Properties** tab at the bottom of the Layers panel. Select the layer and click **Properties**: the heading at the top of the tab confirms which layer you are editing, for example *Layer: Regional Guidance 1*. The settings are in its **Layer** section. The Layer section comes after the settings of the active tool, so **you may need to scroll the Properties pane down to see it**. Dragging the divider above the Properties pane upward, or collapsing the color picker, gives it more room. ### The generation frame [Section titled “The generation frame”](#the-generation-frame) The dashed rectangle on the canvas is the **generation frame**, also called the bounding box. Only the area inside it is generated: what lies inside is the model’s starting point, and the result is placed back in the same spot. The frame’s size is the generation size, and it stays in step with the **Size** section of the Generate panel. Move and resize it with the **Generation frame** tool (press **C**). See [The generation frame](/users-guide/canvas/canvas-guide/#the-generation-frame) for details. ### What Invoke does [Section titled “What Invoke does”](#what-invoke-does) When the Canvas is the source of a generation, InvokeAI looks at what is inside the generation frame and chooses the kind of generation for you: | Inside the frame | Generation | | -------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | No visible raster content | **Text to image**: a new image from the prompt alone. | | Raster content covering the whole frame, no inpaint mask | **Image to image**: the content is repainted. **Denoising strength** in the Generate panel sets how much it changes. | | Raster content covering the frame, and an inpaint mask | **Inpainting**: only the masked area is regenerated. | | Raster content that covers only part of the frame | **Outpainting**: the empty part is filled in, blending into the existing content. | ## Sending generations to the Canvas [Section titled “Sending generations to the Canvas”](#sending-generations-to-the-canvas) In the Edit layout, **Invoke** uses the Canvas as its source and sends the results back to the Canvas. The routing control next to Invoke shows this. Editing the canvas switches the route back to the Canvas automatically, unless the routing is locked. See [Routing images to the Gallery or the Canvas](/users-guide/image-generation/introduction/#routing-images-to-the-gallery-or-the-canvas). When the source is the Canvas, the **Size** section’s width and height are the frame’s, and **Render at** at the bottom of the section chooses the size the model generates at before the result is scaled back to the frame (legacy versions called this *Scale before processing*): the frame’s own size, the model’s optimal size, or a custom size. The **Render** section adds **Denoising strength** below the guidance scale: how much image-to-image, inpainting and outpainting may change the existing content. The default is 75%, and the section header shows the current value. The Generate panel also adds a **Compositing** section at the bottom, which sets how inpainted and outpainted areas are filled and blended: **Infill method**, **Coherence pass mode**, **Coherence edge size**, **Coherence min denoise** and **Mask blur**. Results do not go straight onto the canvas. They appear in the **staging area**, a bar at the bottom of the canvas where you can step through the candidates, then **Accept to Layer** the one you want (it becomes a new raster layer), **Save to gallery**, or **Discard**. While results are staged, the canvas tools are locked except for **View**. ## Inpainting [Section titled “Inpainting”](#inpainting) Inpainting regenerates part of an image and leaves the rest untouched: remove an object, fix a face, or change what is in a corner. ![An inpaint mask, shown as a red overlay, painted over a rock in a mountain landscape.](/_astro/canvas-inpaint.D76mSS0Z_ZNHtcF.webp) 1. **Add an inpaint mask**, or select the one a new canvas starts with, in the **Inpaint Masks** stack. 2. **Paint the mask.** Choose the **Brush** (**B**) and paint over the area to regenerate, or draw it with the **Shape** tool (**R**). The mask shows as a tinted overlay. The **Eraser** (**E**) removes mask, and **\[** and **]** change the brush size. 3. **Describe the result** in the Generate panel’s prompt: describe the whole picture as it should look, or just what should appear in the masked area. 4. **Press Invoke**, then pick a result in the staging area and click **Accept to Layer**. ![Inpainting a plate of sushi: on the left, an inpaint mask over one piece; on the right, the result in the staging area, where that piece has become salmon-roe sushi, ready for Accept to Layer.](/_astro/canvas-inpaint-result.DyC26D3o_Z16Xe9Q.webp) **Denoising strength** controls how much the masked area may change: lower values keep its colors and shapes, higher values replace it. Two optional modifiers, added from the mask’s right-click menu, give finer control: **Add noise** adds noise inside the mask before generating, and **Add denoise limit** caps how strongly it can be repainted. The mask’s **Invert mask** button, in its Properties, swaps the masked and unmasked areas. ## Outpainting [Section titled “Outpainting”](#outpainting) Outpainting extends an image beyond its edges. ![The generation frame extended to the right of the landscape image, leaving an empty area to be filled.](/_astro/canvas-outpaint.BvmGuPxS_2cEa8X.webp) 1. **Choose the Generation frame tool** (press **C**). 2. **Extend the frame** past the edge of the image by dragging its handles, or type a new width and height in the **Frame** section of the Properties pane. Part of the frame now covers empty canvas. 3. **Press Invoke.** The empty area is filled first, using the **Infill method** in the Generate panel’s **Compositing** section, and then generated so that it blends into the existing image. Include some of the existing image in the frame, since the model uses it to continue the scene. You can combine outpainting with an inpaint mask to regenerate part of the existing image at the same time. ## Regional prompts and reference images [Section titled “Regional prompts and reference images”](#regional-prompts-and-reference-images) Regional guidance gives one area of the image its own prompt. For example, keep the main prompt for the landscape and add birds only in the sky. ![A regional guidance layer, shown in green over the sky, with the prompt "a flock of birds soaring over the peaks" in the Layer section of the Properties pane.](/_astro/canvas-regional-guidance.Dm9UQBAZ_1XI45Y.webp) 1. **Add a Regional guidance layer** with **+ → Regional guidance**. 2. **Paint the region** with the **Brush**, or draw it with the **Shape** tool. It shows as a tinted overlay. 3. **Enter the region’s prompt.** With the layer selected, open **Properties** and scroll down to its **Layer** section. Type in **Positive prompt**, and optionally **Negative prompt**. The prompt is saved when you click away from the field. 4. **Press Invoke.** The main prompt still describes the whole image; the regional prompt applies inside the region. To guide a region with an image instead of, or as well as, words, choose **Add reference image** from the regional guidance layer’s right-click menu, or add a **Regional reference image** layer from the **+** menu. The reference appears as a row under the layer; select that row to choose its image, model and weight in Properties. Regional guidance works with SD 1.5, SDXL, FLUX.1, FLUX.2, Krea-2, Z-Image and Anima. Regional negative prompts are available for SD 1.5 and SDXL, and regional reference images for SD 1.5, SDXL (IP-Adapter) and FLUX.1 (FLUX Redux). With other models, regional layers are skipped, and the layer’s Properties say so. For a reference image that applies to the whole picture, use **Add reference image** in the Generate panel instead. ## Control layers [Section titled “Control layers”](#control-layers) A control layer shapes the composition with a guide image: the edges of a sketch, the depth of a scene, or a person’s pose. A control model makes the generated image follow it. ![A control layer's settings in the Layer section of Properties: Adapter type ControlNet, Model Depth Map, and Weight 0.75.](/_astro/canvas-control-layer.BF1df1nv_ZKhHJd.webp) 1. **Put the guide image on a control layer.** A control layer’s image is its own pixels; there is no separate image picker. Do one of these: * Right-click a raster layer and choose **Copy to → Copy to control layer**, or **Convert to → Convert to control layer**. * Drag an image from the Gallery onto the canvas and drop it on **Add as Control Layer** (see [below](#adding-a-gallery-image-to-a-layer)). * Add an empty **Control layer** from the **+** menu and draw on it. 2. **Choose the model.** Select the layer, open **Properties** and scroll to its **Layer** section. Choose the **Adapter type** (ControlNet, T2I Adapter, Control LoRA or Z-Image ControlNet) and the **Model**. A compatible installed model is chosen for you when the layer is created. 3. **Process the image, if needed.** Most control models expect a processed image, such as an edge map or a depth map, rather than a photograph. Choosing a model starts its recommended **Filter** automatically; you can also click **Filter**, pick a filter, and **Apply** it. 4. **Adjust the influence** with **Weight** (how strongly the guide is followed), **Step range** (which part of the generation it applies to) and, for ControlNet, **Control mode**. Then press Invoke. Control layers work with SD 1.5, SDXL, FLUX.1 and Z-Image, and need a control model for the same family, installed from the Model Manager’s starter models. If the **Model** list is empty, no compatible model is installed for the model selected in the Generate panel. A control layer without a model stops Invoke with the message *Select a control model before generating.* ## Drawing on a raster layer [Section titled “Drawing on a raster layer”](#drawing-on-a-raster-layer) You can paint directly on the canvas, for example to sketch a composition for image-to-image, or to touch up a result. 1. **Select a raster layer** in the Layers panel, or add one with **+ → Raster layer**. If you start painting with no suitable layer selected, a new raster layer is created for you. 2. **Pick a color** in the color picker at the top of the Layers panel. Its two chips are the foreground color, used by the brush, and the background color. **X** swaps them and **D** resets them to black and white. Hold **Alt** to pick a color from the canvas. 3. **Choose the Brush** (**B**) and paint. Its **Size**, **Opacity** and **Hardness** are in the Properties pane; **\[** and **]** change the size. The **Eraser** (**E**) erases. The tool strip also has shape, gradient and text tools, which are described in the [Canvas guide](/users-guide/canvas/canvas-guide/). ## Adding a gallery image to a layer [Section titled “Adding a gallery image to a layer”](#adding-a-gallery-image-to-a-layer) There are three ways to bring an existing image onto the canvas: * **Drag it from the Gallery.** With the Gallery and the Canvas both on screen (for example, the Compose layout with its center view switched to Canvas), drag an image onto the canvas. Drop zones appear: **Add as Raster Layer**, **Add as Control Layer**, **Add as Regional Reference Image**, **Add as Inpaint Mask** and **Add as Resized Control Layer**, which scales the image to the model’s optimal size. * **Use the image’s menu.** Right-click an image in the Gallery or Preview and choose **Add to Current Canvas**, then the kind of layer. **New Project from Image** instead starts a new project whose canvas holds the image, sized to fit it; the current project is left as it is. * **Paste it.** Copy an image, click the canvas and press **Ctrl+V** (**Cmd+V** on macOS). It is added as a new raster layer at the generation frame. A new raster layer from an image is placed at its full size at the top-left of the generation frame. Use the **Move** (**V**) or **Transform** (**Ctrl+T**) tool to position and scale it.

# Layers panel guide

> A detailed guide to the Canvas Layers panel — the color picker, managing layers, history, the layer menu, and every layer type's settings in the Properties pane.

The **Layers** panel sits to the right of the Canvas in the **Edit** layout. It has three parts, from top to bottom: 1. **Color** — the color picker and swatches used by the painting tools. 2. **Layers** and **History** — the canvas’s layers, or its undo history. 3. **Properties**, **Transform** and **Overview** — the settings of the active tool and of the selected layer. Drag the dividers between the parts to resize them, and use the chevron at the right of the Color and Properties tabs to collapse them. The sizes are saved with the project. ![The Layers panel: the color wheel at the top, the layer list grouped into Inpaint Masks, Regional Guidance, Control Layers and Raster Layers, and the Properties pane showing a control layer's Adapter type, Model and Weight.](/_astro/layers-panel.CK3ltuzZ_Z2uSWIt.webp) For an introduction to the layer types, see [Crafting images with the Canvas](/users-guide/canvas/introduction/#canvas-concepts). ## Color [Section titled “Color”](#color) The **Color** tab edits the two painting colors: the **Foreground color**, which the brush and text use, and the **Background color**. Click a chip to choose which one you are editing. * The color wheel, or a box picker via **Switch to box picker**, and a field for the value. The format button cycles through hex, RGB, HSL and HSB. * **Swap foreground and background colors** (**X**) and **Reset colors to black and white** (**D**). * **Pick a color from the canvas** — the eyedropper. You can also hold **Alt** on the canvas. A magnifying loupe shows the pixel under the pointer and its RGB values; see the [Canvas guide](/users-guide/canvas/canvas-guide/#tools). * When an inpaint mask or regional guidance layer is selected, a third chip, **Mask tint**, edits the color of its overlay. The **Swatches** tab has built-in **Swatches**, your **Recent colors**, and the **Project palette**: click **+** (**Add current color to palette**) to save a color with the project, and right-click a swatch to remove it. ## Layers [Section titled “Layers”](#layers) ### The layer list [Section titled “The layer list”](#the-layer-list) Layers are grouped into four stacks: **Inpaint Masks**, **Regional Guidance**, **Control Layers** and **Raster Layers**. Within a stack, higher layers are drawn over lower ones. Click a stack’s header to collapse it. Its buttons add a **New layer** of that type and, for masks, regional guidance and control layers, **Hide all** or **Show all**. The Raster Layers header also has **Merge visible** and **Export to PSD**. Each row shows, from left to right: * A colored stripe, if you gave the layer a color label. * A dot that turns the layer on or off (**Enable/disable layer**). A disabled layer takes no part in generation. * A thumbnail, the layer type and the name. * An eye button (**Show/hide layer**) on masks, regional guidance and control layers. It only hides the layer from view; a hidden layer still affects generation. * A lock button (**Toggle lock**), which prevents editing. Rows can have child rows, shown with a chevron: adjustments and regenerate regions on raster layers, noise and denoise limits on inpaint masks, and reference images on regional guidance layers. Select a child row to edit it in Properties. Drag an adjustment to reorder it, or drop it on another raster layer or group, or among that layer’s adjustments, to move it there as one undoable step. Reference images move between regional guidance layers the same way. A child row’s right-click menu also has a **Move to layer** submenu listing the layers that can take it. ### Working with layers [Section titled “Working with layers”](#working-with-layers) * **Add** a layer with the **+** button next to the Layers and History tabs, or by right-clicking empty space in the list. The new layer is placed above the selected one and selected. * **Select** a layer by clicking it. **Ctrl**-click adds or removes layers from the selection, and **Shift**-click selects a range. * **Rename** a layer by double-clicking its name or pressing **F2**. **Enter** saves and **Escape** cancels. * **Reorder** layers by dragging them, or with **Alt+↑** and **Alt+↓**. Layers can only move within their own stack. * **Blend mode** and **Opacity**, in the row above the list, apply to the selected layer. There are 16 blend modes, from Normal and Multiply to Color and Luminosity. * **Group** layers into folders with **Group selected layers**, or **Ctrl+G** on the canvas. **Alt+→** moves a layer into the group above it and **Alt+←** moves it out. A group’s dot, eye and lock apply to everything in it. * **Filter layers** at the bottom of the list shows only the layers whose names match. * The buttons beside the filter **Duplicate selected layers**, **Group selected layers** and **Delete selected layers**. ## History [Section titled “History”](#history) The **History** tab lists the canvas’s edits, oldest first, with the current step highlighted and undone steps in italics. Click a step to go back or forward to it, or use the **Undo** and **Redo** buttons (**Ctrl+Z**, and **Ctrl+Shift+Z** or **Ctrl+Y**). ![The History tab listing the canvas's recent edits, such as Brush stroke, Regional guidance and Positive prompt.](/_astro/layers-history._7twDXiF_Z2bMUwi.webp) The history keeps the last 64 steps. It lasts only while the project is open in your browser: reloading the page, or starting a new canvas, clears it. ## The layer menu [Section titled “The layer menu”](#the-layer-menu) Right-click a layer, or select it and press **Shift+F10**, for its menu. Right-clicking the canvas opens the same menu for the selected layer. ![The menu of a raster layer, with Transform, Rename layer, Fit to bbox, Add adjustment, Add regenerate region, Filter, Select object, Merge down, Copy to, Convert to, Crop layer to bbox, Save layer to uploads, Disable layer, Lock layer, Color label and Delete layer.](/_astro/layers-context-menu.Dj9MrUdb_Z2vnFk0.webp) The icons at the top **Arrange** the layer (move it to the front, forward, backward or to the back), **Duplicate layer** and **Group layers**. Below them: * **For every layer:** * **Rename layer** and **Fit to bbox** (scale the layer to fit inside the generation frame). * **Merge down**. * **Copy to** — including **Copy layer to clipboard**, and copies to other layer types. * **Crop layer to bbox** and **Save layer to uploads** (save it to the Gallery’s Uploads). * **Disable layer**, **Lock layer** and **Color label**. * **Delete layer**. * **Raster layers:** * **Transform**. * **Add adjustment** — Brightness/Contrast, Exposure, Levels, Curves, Saturation, Hue or Invert. Adjustments are non-destructive and appear as child rows. * **Add regenerate region** — treats the layer’s own shape as an inpaint mask. * **Filter**, **Select object** and **Run workflow** — process the layer; see the [Canvas guide](/users-guide/canvas/canvas-guide/#filters-and-object-selection). * **Boolean operations** — combine the layer with the one below: intersect, cut out, cut away or exclude. * **Convert to** — make it a control layer, inpaint mask or regional guidance layer. Text, shape and gradient layers can also be rasterized into plain pixels. * **Control layers:** **Transform**, **Filter**, **Select object**, **Run workflow**, **Enable transparent preview**, and **Convert to raster layer**. * **Inpaint masks:** **Add noise**, **Add denoise limit**, **Extract masked area** (copy the masked part of the image to a new layer), and **Hide layer**. * **Regional guidance:** **Enable auto-negative**, **Add reference image**, and **Hide layer**. When several layers are selected, the menu also offers **Merge selected layers**. ## Properties [Section titled “Properties”](#properties) A heading at the top of the **Properties** tab names what it is editing: **Layer:** or **Group:** followed by the selected layer’s or group’s name, **Operation:** followed by the operation’s name while a Filter or Select Object operation runs, or *No layer selected*. It stays in view as you scroll, so you can always tell which layer the settings below belong to. Below the heading, the tab shows up to three sections, in this order: 1. The running operation’s settings — while a **Filter** or **Select Object** operation is running. Starting either from a layer’s menu opens the Layers panel on this tab. 2. **Tool** — the options of the active canvas tool; see the [Canvas guide](/users-guide/canvas/canvas-guide/#tool-options). 3. **Layer** — the settings of the selected layer. The Layer section is dimmed while results are being staged or a canvas generation is running. ### Raster layer [Section titled “Raster layer”](#raster-layer) * **Lock transparency** — paint only where the layer already has pixels, leaving transparent areas transparent, like Photoshop’s “Lock transparent pixels”. Use it to recolor a shape without spilling paint around it, or to refine a subject painted on a transparent layer without growing its outline. Brushes, shapes and pen input all respect the lock. * **Filter** — start the Filter operation. Adjustment child rows each have their own settings, such as **Brightness** and **Contrast**, **Exposure**, **Levels** and **Curves** with a channel selector, **Saturation**, and **Hue**. A regenerate region has a **Fill color** and **Fill style**. ### Control layer [Section titled “Control layer”](#control-layer) * **Adapter type** — ControlNet, T2I Adapter, Control LoRA, Z-Image ControlNet or Anima ControlNet-LLLite, depending on the model selected in the Generate panel. * **Model** — the installed control models of that type for the same model family. If the list is empty, install one from the starter models. For Anima, the list holds the LLLite control adapters but not the Inpainting adapter, and each LLLite model can drive only one control layer per generation. * **Weight** — how strongly the guide is followed (0 to 2; the default is 0.75 for ControlNet). * **Step range** — the part of the generation, from start to finish, in which the guide applies. * **Control mode** (ControlNet only) — **Balanced**, **More prompt**, **More control** or **Unbalanced**. * **Transparent preview** — shows the layer semi-transparently over the image. * **Filter** — process the layer’s image into a guide, such as an edge or depth map. The control image is the layer’s own pixels. To use a picture, copy or convert a raster layer, or drop a gallery image on **Add as Control Layer**. ### Inpaint mask [Section titled “Inpaint mask”](#inpaint-mask) * **Fill color** and **Fill style** (Solid, Grid, Crosshatch, Diagonal, Horizontal or Vertical) — how the mask is drawn on screen. * **Invert mask** — swap the masked and unmasked areas. Its child rows, added from the layer menu, set **Noise** (noise added inside the mask before generating, 25% by default) and **Denoise limit** (the most the masked area may change, 80% by default). ### Regional guidance [Section titled “Regional guidance”](#regional-guidance) * **Positive prompt** and **Negative prompt** — the prompts for this region. Each is saved when you click away from the field. The negative prompt is shown only for models that use one. * **Auto-Negative** — also uses the region’s positive prompt as a negative prompt outside the region. * **Fill color**, **Fill style** and **Invert mask**, as for inpaint masks. If the selected model does not support regional guidance, a message says that the layer is skipped during generation. ### Regional reference image [Section titled “Regional reference image”](#regional-reference-image) A regional guidance layer’s reference image is a child row. Select it to set: * The image: **Choose image** from the Gallery, drop a gallery image on it, or **Upload** a file. * **Model** — an IP-Adapter (SD 1.5, SDXL) or FLUX Redux (FLUX.1) model. * For IP-Adapter, **Method** (Full, Style, Composition, Style (strong) or Style (precise)) and **Weight**. For FLUX Redux, **Image influence**. ## Transform and Overview [Section titled “Transform and Overview”](#transform-and-overview) The **Transform** tab sets the selected layer’s **Position**, **Scale** and **Rotation** as numbers. Each change is a separate undoable step. The **Overview** tab shows a thumbnail of the whole canvas with the visible area outlined. Click it to move the view. ## Keyboard shortcuts [Section titled “Keyboard shortcuts”](#keyboard-shortcuts) In the layer list: | Shortcut | Action | | --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | | **↑** / **↓**, **Home** / **End** | Move between layers | | **→** / **←** | Expand / collapse, or go to the parent group | | **Enter** or **Space** | Select | | **F2** | Rename | | **Delete** / **Backspace** | Delete the layer | | **Ctrl+C** | Copy the layer to the clipboard | | **Alt+↑** / **Alt+↓** | Move the layer up / down | | **Alt+→** / **Alt+←** | Move into the group above / out of its group | | **Shift+F10** | Open the layer menu | | **Ctrl+Z** / **Ctrl+Shift+Z** | Undo / redo | On macOS, use **Cmd** in place of **Ctrl**. More layer shortcuts, such as duplicate, merge and arrange, work while the canvas has focus; see the [Canvas guide](/users-guide/canvas/canvas-guide/#keyboard-shortcuts).

# Gallery Reference

> Details of the Gallery — the board menu, archiving, downloading and deleting boards, the media menu, Gallery settings and keyboard shortcuts.

This page describes the Gallery’s menus, settings and shortcuts in detail. For an introduction to boards, searching, starring, uploading, and moving and deleting media, see [Organizing your media](/users-guide/gallery/introduction/). ## Managing boards [Section titled “Managing boards”](#managing-boards) ### The board menu [Section titled “The board menu”](#the-board-menu) Hover over a board and click its **⋮** button, or right-click it, to open its menu: ![The board menu with Auto-add to this board, Download Board, Rename board, Archive Board and Delete Board.](/_astro/gallery-board-menu.De5i8f4e_ZrBd8v.webp) * **Auto-add to this board** — makes this the board that receives new results, marked **Auto**, whichever board is selected. On the auto-add board, the item is **Stop auto-adding here**, which goes back to sending results to the selected board. Not offered for date boards or archived boards. See [Choosing where new media goes](/users-guide/gallery/introduction/#choosing-where-new-media-goes). * **Download Board** — downloads the board (see [below](#downloading-a-board)). * **Rename board** — opens a dialog to change the name. * **Move to…** — moves the board to the **Library**, into the open project, or into one of your other projects. A board in a project is private to you, so this is offered only for your own private boards: a shared or public board stays in the **Library**, and an administrator cannot move another person’s boards. You can also drag the board onto another group: the open project’s, the **Library**, or one of your projects under **Other projects**. When the board’s new project is hidden because **Other projects’ boards** is off: if it was the selected board, the Gallery selects **Uncategorized**; if it was the auto-add board, results follow the selected board again. * **Archive Board** / **Unarchive Board** — see [below](#archiving-a-board). * **Delete Board** — see [below](#deleting-a-board). A project’s **Inbox** is managed through its project: its menu has **Export project (.invk)**, **Auto-add to this board** and **Download Board** instead, and renaming the project renames it. **Uncategorized** offers only **Auto-add to this board** and **Download Board**, and date boards have no menu. If the auto-add board is deleted, results go back to following the selected board. The same happens when you open a project after a board it used was deleted elsewhere — in another tab, or together with a project deleted from the Launchpad: the project stops selecting it, auto-adding to it and sending queued results to it. ### Archiving a board [Section titled “Archiving a board”](#archiving-a-board) Archiving hides a board you no longer use without deleting anything. Choose **Archive Board** from its menu, and the board disappears from the list. To see archived boards again, turn on **Archived boards** in the **Filter & sort boards** menu; they appear in their own **Archived** group, where **Unarchive Board** returns them to the list. Archived boards are not included in [semantic search](/users-guide/gallery/introduction/#searching-by-content). ### Downloading a board [Section titled “Downloading a board”](#downloading-a-board) **Download Board** packages the board’s images, from both its Media and Uploads tabs, into a `.zip` file. A notice appears while the archive is prepared, and the browser saves the file when it is ready. Videos are not included, and the menu item says how many will be left out, for example **Download Board (1 video omitted)**. To save a video, download it on its own from its menu. ### Deleting a board [Section titled “Deleting a board”](#deleting-a-board) Choose **Delete Board** from the board’s menu. The confirmation dialog shows how many images, videos and uploads the board holds, and offers two choices: ![The Delete board dialog with Cancel, Delete Board Only and Delete Board and Media buttons.](/_astro/gallery-delete-board.BSMSU8er_1Hpr9O.webp) * **Delete Board Only** — removes the board and moves everything on it to **Uncategorized**. * **Delete Board and Media** — removes the board and **permanently deletes** its images and videos. Danger **Delete Board and Media** cannot be undone. Queued or running jobs that were sending results to the deleted board send them to **Uncategorized** instead. A project’s Inbox cannot be deleted from the Gallery; delete the project instead, which also asks what to do with the project’s other boards. On a multi-user installation, only a board’s owner or an administrator can delete it. When an owner deletes a shared board with its media, only their own media is deleted and other people’s items move to Uncategorized; an administrator’s deletion removes everything. If some files cannot be removed, those items are kept in Uncategorized and a warning says how many. ## The media menu [Section titled “The media menu”](#the-media-menu) Right-click an item, or several selected items, for its menu. ![The context menu for an image, with quick-action icons at the top followed by Load Workflow, Recall Metadata, Add to Current Canvas, New Project from Image, Send to Upscale, Send to Video, Use as Reference Image, Use as Prompt Template, Select for Compare, Find in Gallery, Change Board and Delete Image.](/_astro/gallery-image-menu.B431dV-6_Z1Q7mx8.webp) For an image, the menu offers: * **Quick actions** (the icons at the top) — open in a new tab, copy to the clipboard, download, open in the Preview, and star. * **Load Workflow** and **Recall Metadata** — restore the workflow or the settings that made the image. Recall Metadata includes **Recall All**, **Remix Image**, **Use Prompt**, **Use Seed**, **Use Size** and **Use CLIP Skip**; see [Resetting to defaults](/users-guide/image-generation/generate-panel/#resetting-to-defaults). These are unavailable for images without generation metadata. * **Add to Current Canvas** — add the image to the open project’s canvas as a new layer of the kind you choose. * **New Project from Image** — start a new project whose canvas holds the image, sized to fit it. * **Send to Upscale**, **Send to Video**, **Use as Reference Image**, **Use as Prompt Template** and **Select for Compare** — use the image elsewhere in InvokeAI. * **Change Board** and **Delete Image**. A video’s menu has the equivalent actions for video, including **Extend in Video**, **Use as Reference Video** and **Use as Conditioning Clip**. With several items selected, the menu offers the actions that apply to all of them, such as **Star All**, **Download Selection**, **Change Board** and **Delete Selection**; for several images it also leads with **Add to Current Canvas** and **New Project from Images**. Every image generated by InvokeAI also stores its generation metadata inside the file, so the prompt and settings travel with it when you download it. ## Gallery settings [Section titled “Gallery settings”](#gallery-settings) The gear button in the Gallery header opens its settings: ![The Gallery settings popover with Image size, Thumbnails, Always show dimensions, Show in-progress section and Pagination.](/_astro/gallery-settings.ByhC1HBy_Zmw6Ns.webp) * **Image size** — the size of the thumbnails. * **Thumbnails** — **Square** crops thumbnails to squares; **Aspect** shows each item’s full shape. * **Always show dimensions** — shows each item’s width and height on its thumbnail, not only on hover. * **Show in-progress section** — shows generations that are still running at the top of the grid. * **Pagination** — **Infinite** scrolling or numbered **Pages**. **All Gallery settings…** at the bottom opens the full settings. They also include **Send new results to the selected board** (under **Destination**), which is on by default; turn it off to keep sending results to the current destination board, which then becomes the **Auto** board. The full settings also include the sort order and the board visibility and sorting options from the [Filter & sort boards](/users-guide/gallery/introduction/#finding-filtering-and-sorting-boards) menu. All Gallery settings are saved with the project. ## Keyboard shortcuts [Section titled “Keyboard shortcuts”](#keyboard-shortcuts) These work while the Gallery has focus: | Shortcut | Action | | -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | | Arrow keys | Move through the grid | | **Enter** / double-click | Open the item in the Preview | | **Shift**-click / **Ctrl**-click | Select a range / add or remove an item | | **Ctrl+A** | Select everything loaded on the page | | **Escape** | Clear the selection | | **.** (period) | Star or unstar the selection | | **Delete** / **Backspace** | Delete the selection | | **R** | Remix the selected image: recall its settings, except the seed | On macOS, use **Cmd** in place of **Ctrl**. See [Hotkeys](/users-guide/workbench/hotkeys/) for all shortcuts.

# Image Storage Maintenance

> Move existing images into the current image subfolder strategy with crash recovery.

InvokeAI can move existing images into the folder layout selected by [`image_subfolder_strategy`](/configuration/invokeai-yaml/#image-subfolder-strategy). This is useful after changing the image subfolder strategy from `flat` to `date`, `type`, or `hash`, or when reorganizing an older image library. This operation changes where image files and thumbnails are stored on disk. It does not change image names, boards, generation metadata, or gallery records. ## Access [Section titled “Access”](#access) Image storage maintenance is available from the in-application Settings panel. Administrators can start image moves, force recovery, and inspect the current move status. If multi-user mode is disabled, the single local user has the same access. Non-admin users in multi-user mode cannot run or inspect image move status. ## Maintenance Mode [Section titled “Maintenance Mode”](#maintenance-mode) Image moves run as a maintenance operation. Before a move starts, InvokeAI checks that no queue work is active. While the move is running, InvokeAI prevents image reads, uploads, deletes, generation jobs, and gallery mutations from racing with the filesystem move. The UI shows the move or recovery state until the job is complete or requires manual attention. Gallery images and thumbnails may be unavailable while maintenance is active. ## Crash Recovery [Section titled “Crash Recovery”](#crash-recovery) The move process is crash-recoverable. InvokeAI records each move job in its database before moving files, moves full-size images and thumbnails on disk, and updates `images.image_subfolder` only after the filesystem move succeeds. If InvokeAI stops during a move, recovery resumes incomplete jobs. If recovery finds an ambiguous filesystem state, such as both the old and new full-size image files existing or neither file existing, it halts that item for manual repair instead of blindly updating the database. Other items in the same job are still finalized, and the maintenance lock is released when the job is recorded as failed. Recovery finalizes jobs that were already recorded before the stop. Images that had not yet been planned into a move job are not moved by recovery itself. The Settings panel reports how many images still need moving; run **Start Move** again to continue. Missing intermediate image files are treated as already cleaned up and do not halt the move. Missing non-intermediate image files, unreadable images, and truncated images are recorded as failed items. When the full-size file is still at its original path, recovery leaves it there so it can be repaired or removed safely. If a previous filesystem move already placed the full-size file at its destination, recovery keeps that destination and reconciles the database before recording the item as failed. After recovery releases the lock, back up the failed file and either replace it with a valid image or delete its image record from the gallery, then run **Start Move** again if images still need moving. Do not delete an active journal row or edit `images.image_subfolder` while maintenance is active. For the `date` strategy, existing images are moved according to their original image creation timestamp stored in the database, not according to the time the maintenance job is run. Empty source directories left behind by successful moves are removed when safe.

# Organizing your media

> Use the Gallery to organize images and videos into boards, choose where new results go, search by metadata or by content, upload media, and move, star, download or delete it.

The **Gallery** holds every image and video you generate or upload. It is organized into **boards**. Every board belongs either to a project — each has an **Inbox** for new results, plus any boards you add to it — or to the **Library**, whose boards are available from every project and include the always-present **Uncategorized** board. From the Gallery you choose where new results go, find media by its prompt or by what it shows, and move, star, download or delete it. ![The Gallery with the Concept Art board selected: the board list at the top, the Media and Uploads tabs, the search field, and a grid of images with starred items pinned at the top.](/_astro/gallery-overview.B1D8pSrO_ZqNESK.webp) ## The Gallery at a glance [Section titled “The Gallery at a glance”](#the-gallery-at-a-glance) The Gallery has three parts: * **The header** shows the selected board after *Gallery /*. Click the board name to hide or show the board list. The gear button opens the [Gallery settings](/users-guide/gallery/gallery-reference/#gallery-settings). * **The board list** has a search field (**Search or create boards**), a **Filter & sort boards** button, and the boards themselves, grouped under the open project’s name, **Library** and, when turned on, **Other projects**, **By Date** and **Archived**. Each group can be collapsed; the project group shows how many boards it has, its Inbox included, the **Library** how many it has besides **Uncategorized**, and **Other projects** how many projects it lists. * **The media area** shows the contents of the selected board, on two tabs: * **Media** — images and videos generated in InvokeAI. * **Uploads** — images, videos and audio you have uploaded. Above the grid are the **Search items** field, the **Starred only** filter, the sort order (**Newest** or **Oldest**) and the upload button. When the Gallery is narrow, or docked in a side rail, the board list sits above the media grid. When it is wide, the board list becomes a column on the left. Drag the divider between them to resize the list. Each board shows its cover image, its name and a count such as **76 | 12**: 76 items on the Media tab and 12 on the Uploads tab. A project’s Inbox is pinned at the top of its group with an inbox icon. On a multi-user installation, other people’s boards show their owner’s name. ## Boards [Section titled “Boards”](#boards) ### Creating a board [Section titled “Creating a board”](#creating-a-board) Type a name into **Search or create boards**. If no board has that name, a **Create board ”…” in …** row appears in both the open project’s group and the **Library** group; click the one where the board should live, or press **Enter** to create it in the project. Each of those two groups also has a **+** button, which asks for the board’s name and creates it in that group; anything already typed in the search field is filled in for you. ![Typing Seascapes into the board search field shows a Create board "Seascapes" row.](/_astro/gallery-create-board.DIKpfpQP_Z2jamvr.webp) The new board is selected straight away, so it also becomes the destination for new results. A board’s cover is chosen automatically: its newest starred item, or its newest item if nothing is starred. ### Choosing where new media goes [Section titled “Choosing where new media goes”](#choosing-where-new-media-goes) **By default, new results go to the board that is selected in the Gallery**: select a board, press **Invoke**, and the results land on that board. The destination is fixed when you press Invoke, so you can select another board and queue more work while earlier jobs are still running, without redirecting them. * A new project starts with its Inbox selected. See [Projects](/users-guide/projects/introduction/#where-your-images-go). * If you select a date board (see below), results go to the project’s Inbox, because date boards are only a view. * Uploads go to the selected board. * If you archive or delete the selected board, the selection, and with it the destination, moves to **Uncategorized**. To keep sending results to one board while you browse others, make it the **auto-add board**: choose **Auto-add to this board** from its menu. The board is marked **Auto**, and new generations, Canvas saves, pasted media and the results of workflow nodes whose **Board** is set to **Auto** all go there, whichever board you are viewing. Choose **Stop auto-adding here** from the same menu to go back to following the selected board. The setting behind this is **Send new results to the selected board**, in the [Gallery settings](/users-guide/gallery/gallery-reference/#gallery-settings). ### Finding, filtering and sorting boards [Section titled “Finding, filtering and sorting boards”](#finding-filtering-and-sorting-boards) Typing in **Search or create boards** narrows the list to boards whose names contain the text. Selecting a board clears the search. The **Filter & sort boards** button beside the search field controls which boards are listed and in what order: ![The Filter & sort boards menu with Board visibility options (Date boards, Archived boards, Other projects' boards) and Sort by options.](/_astro/gallery-board-filters.BflyWf7S_1jK6iH.webp) * **Board visibility** * **Date boards** — adds a **By Date** group with one board per day on which you created media. Date boards are read-only views: you cannot upload to them, drop media on them, or rename or delete them. * **Archived boards** — adds an **Archived** group listing the boards you have archived. * **Other projects’ boards** — adds an **Other projects** group with your other projects’ boards, grouped by project. They are hidden by default to keep the list focused; the open project’s boards are always shown. * **Sort by** — **Created** (the default) or **Name**, in descending or ascending order. Each project’s **Inbox** and the Library’s **Uncategorized** always stay at the top of their group. These choices are saved with the project, so each project can list boards differently. ### Renaming, archiving, downloading and deleting boards [Section titled “Renaming, archiving, downloading and deleting boards”](#renaming-archiving-downloading-and-deleting-boards) Right-click a board, or hover over it and click its **⋯** button, to rename, move, archive, download or delete it. [Managing boards](/users-guide/gallery/gallery-reference/#managing-boards) in the Gallery Reference describes each action, including what deleting a board does to its media. ## Finding media in a board [Section titled “Finding media in a board”](#finding-media-in-a-board) Search, the starred filter and the sort order apply to the selected board and the current tab (Media or Uploads). ### Searching by metadata [Section titled “Searching by metadata”](#searching-by-metadata) Type into **Search items** to find media whose generation metadata contains the text, such as a word from the prompt, a model name or a seed. The search is not case-sensitive and matches the text exactly as typed, spaces included. Media without metadata, such as most uploads, can only be found by date. To limit results by date, add a date token. The **?** button in the search field shows the syntax: ![The Search syntax help, listing the from:, to: and date: tokens with examples.](/_astro/gallery-search-help.8LM__oMi_ZiIBoE.webp) * `from:` — on or after a day, e.g. `from:2026-07-14` * `to:` — on or before a day, e.g. `to:yesterday` * `date:` — a single day, e.g. `date:today` Days can be written as `YYYY-MM-DD`, `today`, `yesterday`, or relative to today: `7d`, `2w` and `1m` mean 7 days, 2 weeks and 1 month ago. For example, `lighthouse from:2w` finds media from the last two weeks whose metadata mentions a lighthouse. A token that cannot be read is shown in red. ### Searching by content [Section titled “Searching by content”](#searching-by-content) When image indexing is turned on, the Gallery can also search by what media *shows*, whatever the prompt said: find “sunset on the beach” even in images that were never prompted with those words. This **semantic search** uses the same index as the [Image Map](/users-guide/image-map/introduction/). To turn indexing on, install the `DFN2B-CLIP-ViT-L-14-39B` model from the starter models and restart the backend; see [Activating the Image Map](/users-guide/image-map/introduction/#activating-the-image-map). When indexing is turned off, the semantic search button is not shown. ![A semantic search for "a wizard holding a torch", with the most similar images first.](/_astro/gallery-semantic-search.CzQ-MSt0_2mJkTO.webp) * **Search by text.** Click the sparkle button at the right end of the search field (**Search semantically**). The field changes to **Describe what to find…**; describe what you are looking for. Any text already in the field is used straight away. * **Search by image.** Drag an image onto the search field: a thumbnail from the Gallery, an image from the Preview, an image file from your computer, or an image from another browser tab. The Gallery then shows the media most similar to it, labelled **Similar to …**. Results are ranked by similarity, most similar first, up to 500 items from the selected board. Videos are included. The Media and Uploads tabs, the sort order, the starred filter and date tokens do not apply to ranked results. To leave semantic search, click the **✕** in the search field, click the sparkle button again (**Exit semantic search**), or switch tabs. If the index model is not installed, the Gallery says so when you try to search. Archived boards are not indexed. ### Sorting and the starred filter [Section titled “Sorting and the starred filter”](#sorting-and-the-starred-filter) The sort menu orders media by creation time, **Newest** first (the default) or **Oldest** first. The star button next to it (**Starred only**) shows only starred items. Images and videos are always shown together. ### Browsing large boards [Section titled “Browsing large boards”](#browsing-large-boards) The media grid continues through the full listing as you scroll, including older items beyond the first few screens. You can also drag the scrollbar to jump to a distant part of the list; the Gallery loads items near that position without first loading every item in between. Scroll back up to browse earlier positions. While a part of the list loads, its tile positions stay in place. If one page cannot be loaded, the Gallery marks its first empty tile with an error and **Retry**, while keeping nearby loaded items available. ## Starring favorites [Section titled “Starring favorites”](#starring-favorites) Star an item to keep it at hand. Hover over a thumbnail and click the star in its corner, choose **Star image** (or **Star video**) from its menu, or select items and press **.** (period). Starred thumbnails keep a yellow star. Starred items are gathered in a **Starred** section at the top of the board, above the rest of the media, which can be collapsed. If there are more than fit, **Show all** switches on the **Starred only** filter. Starring also affects the board’s cover, which is its newest starred item. ## Uploading media [Section titled “Uploading media”](#uploading-media) Click the upload button at the right of the tab bar (**Upload media to …**) and choose files, or drag files from your computer onto the media grid. An empty board also shows **Drop media here or click to upload**. Uploads go to the selected board, on its **Uploads** tab. You cannot upload to a date board. You can upload: * **Images** — PNG, JPEG and WebP. * **Videos** — stored and played as H.264/AAC MP4. H.264 video in another container, such as an iPhone `.mov` recorded as “Most Compatible”, is repackaged almost instantly. Other formats, such as HEVC, ProRes, VP9 and `.wmv`, are converted, which takes roughly as long as the clip on a typical CPU. 10-bit HDR footage is converted to 8-bit without tone mapping, so it will look flatter than the original. * **Audio** — MP3, M4A, WAV, FLAC, OGG and similar files become a video that shows the waveform. It behaves like any other video, for example as the soundtrack for [audio-to-video](/users-guide/video-generation/introduction/) generation. You can also paste an image or video from the clipboard while no text field has focus. A dialog asks whether to upload it to the Gallery, add it to the Canvas, or use it as a reference image. ## Selecting, moving and deleting media [Section titled “Selecting, moving and deleting media”](#selecting-moving-and-deleting-media) Click an item to select it, and double-click it (or press **Enter** while its thumbnail has keyboard focus) to open it in the Preview, in the center of the workbench. **Shift**-click selects a range, and **Ctrl**-click (**Cmd**-click on macOS) adds or removes single items. **Ctrl+A** selects everything loaded on the page, and **Escape** clears the selection. While anything is selected, a bar at the bottom of the Gallery shows how many items are selected, with buttons to star them, move them to another board, download them, or delete them. ![Three selected images with the selection bar at the bottom of the Gallery showing 3 selected.](/_astro/gallery-selection.CIwYGsft_1ORNCF.webp) ### Moving media to another board [Section titled “Moving media to another board”](#moving-media-to-another-board) Drag items onto a board in the board list; if the list is hidden, it opens while you drag. You can also use **Change Board** in an item’s menu, or the move button in the selection bar. Moving never copies: each item is on one board at a time. **Remove from Board** in the **Change Board** menu moves an item to **Uncategorized**. ### Deleting media [Section titled “Deleting media”](#deleting-media) Press **Delete** (or **Backspace**), choose **Delete Image**, **Delete Video** or **Delete Selection** from the menu, or use the delete button in the selection bar. Deleting permanently removes the items from every board and from disk, and cannot be undone. A confirmation asks first. Tick **Don’t ask me again** and confirm to stop asking (cancelling leaves it on); you can turn it back on, or off, with **Confirm image deletion** in Settings under Gallery. Deleting does not check whether an image is still used elsewhere, for example on a canvas or as a reference image, so check before you delete media you are still working with. If deleting is interrupted, InvokeAI cleans up any leftover files the next time it starts. ## Related pages [Section titled “Related pages”](#related-pages) * [Gallery Reference](/users-guide/gallery/gallery-reference/) — the board and media menus, Gallery settings and keyboard shortcuts. * [Image Map](/users-guide/image-map/introduction/) — explore your whole gallery as a map of similar images. * [Image Storage Maintenance](/users-guide/gallery/image-storage-maintenance/) — for administrators: reorganize how image files are stored on disk. * [Intermediates](/users-guide/image-generation/intermediates/) — reclaim space used by temporary files that never reached the Gallery.

# Advanced Prompt Syntax

> Fine control over prompts — attention weighting, blending and conjunctions for SD 1.5, SD 2.x and SDXL, and the advanced dynamic prompt syntax for multiple choices, weights, variables and comments.

Most prompts need nothing more than plain text, perhaps with a [prompt template](/users-guide/image-generation/prompting-guide/#prompt-templates) or a few [dynamic prompt](/users-guide/image-generation/prompting-guide/#dynamic-prompts) alternatives. This page covers the syntax for finer control: making parts of a prompt count for more or less, blending prompts, and the advanced forms of dynamic prompts. ## Attention weighting [Section titled “Attention weighting”](#attention-weighting) Attention weighting makes parts of the prompt count for more or less than the rest. It uses Compel syntax, which applies to **SD 1.5, SD 2.x and SDXL**. Newer model families, including FLUX, Z-Image, CogView4 and Qwen Image, do not use it, and the symbols are passed to the model as ordinary text. | Syntax | Effect | | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | | `trees+` / `fog-` | Increase or decrease a single word | | `(golden hour light)+` | Weight a phrase | | `(cinematic lighting)1.25` | Use an exact numeric weight | | `(portrait with (blue eyes)1.3)1.1` | Nest weights | | `("portrait photo", "oil painting").blend(0.7, 0.3)` | Blend prompts | | `("red silk dress", "studio portrait", "soft rim light").and()` | Encode clauses separately | | `colored pencil \(medium\)` | Use literal parentheses | ### Weighting with `+` and `-` [Section titled “Weighting with + and -”](#weighting-with--and--) Append `+` to increase influence, or `-` to reduce it. 
```text
freckles+
background crowd-
(soft rim light)++
```
 * Single words can be weighted directly. Wrap phrases of several words in parentheses. * Each additional `+` or `-` compounds, in steps of roughly 10%. * One or two steps is usually enough. Extreme weighting can overpower the rest of the prompt. ### Numeric weights [Section titled “Numeric weights”](#numeric-weights) Use numeric weights when you want precise control instead of repeated plus or minus markers. 
```text
(cinematic lighting)1.25
(background crowd)0.8
```
 `1` is neutral, values above `1` increase emphasis, and values between `0` and `1` reduce it. Wrap the weighted phrase in parentheses. Groups can be nested, and the weights combine. In `(portrait with (blue eyes)1.3)1.1`, the outer group strengthens the whole phrase, and `blue eyes` gets even more emphasis. ### Adjusting weights with the keyboard [Section titled “Adjusting weights with the keyboard”](#adjusting-weights-with-the-keyboard) In a prompt field, select text and press **Ctrl+Up** or **Ctrl+Down** to raise or lower its attention. With no selection, the shortcut targets the word at the cursor. Selecting a group’s parentheses or weight targets its contents. * A selection inside a group changes only the selected words. A selection crossing a group boundary changes the selected words on both sides. * Symbolic weights move one `+` or `-` step. Numeric weights change by `0.1` of effective attention, including inherited group weights. * The numeric attention preference controls new weights; existing group weights keep their style. * Adjacent content with matching weights merges, and the adjusted content stays selected for the next keypress. * Inside prompt functions, the shortcut adjusts prompt arguments and preserves function parameters.
